topicTitle: Cell Membrane: Osmosis, Diffusion & Active Transport

objects.label: Passive Diffusion
objects.explanation: Solutes move spontaneously down their concentration gradient from high to low concentration without expending cellular ATP.

objects.label: Osmosis (Water Flow)
objects.explanation: Water diffuses across a selectively permeable membrane toward the side with higher solute concentration.

objects.label: Active Transport Pump
objects.formula: ATP → ADP + Pᵢ (3 Na⁺ out, 2 K⁺ in)
objects.explanation: Carrier pumps hydrolyze ATP to force ions uphill against their electrochemical gradient.

steps.title: Passive Transport: Moving Down the Gradient
steps.narration: In simple and facilitated diffusion, molecules move spontaneously from higher concentration to lower concentration without using metabolic ATP energy.
steps.tutorTip: Tap 'Passive Diffusion' to review why facilitated channel proteins still count as passive.

inlineQuiz.question: Glucose enters a cell down its concentration gradient through a membrane carrier protein without using ATP. What process is this?
inlineQuiz.explanation: Moving down a concentration gradient via a transport protein with zero ATP cost is facilitated diffusion.

steps.title: Osmosis & Solution Tonicity
steps.narration: Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane from a hypotonic (lower solute) region to a hypertonic (higher solute) region.
steps.tutorTip: Remember: 'Salt sucks'—water flows toward the higher solute concentration.

inlineQuiz.question: What happens to a red blood cell placed in a strongly hypertonic salt solution?
options: Water leaves the cell and it shrivels (crenates)
Water rushes into the cell and it bursts (lyses)
Salt is pumped out using ATP
No net movement of water occurs
inlineQuiz.explanation: Because the outside solution is hypertonic (higher solute), water moves out of the cell by osmosis, causing it to shrivel.

steps.title: Active Transport: Pumping Against the Gradient
steps.narration: When a cell must concentrate ions against their gradient (from low to high), transmembrane pumps hydrolyze ATP—such as the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase pumping 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in.
steps.tutorTip: Tap 'Active Transport Pump' to inspect the stoichiometry of the sodium-potassium pump.

inlineQuiz.question: Which feature distinguishes active transport from facilitated diffusion?
options: It moves solutes against their concentration gradient using ATP
It moves water molecules down a gradient
It occurs without a cell membrane
inlineQuiz.explanation: Both use membrane proteins, but only active transport moves solutes uphill against their gradient using ATP.
